title: Microsoft Edge: Rewrite by Copilot (Writing Assistance) gains enterprise data protection
summary: Hold: the DLP command creates a policy container but does not configure the sensitive service domain groups or blocking rules shown beside it. The page also overstates availability on unprotected pages; the default-on announcement, roadmap facts and documented Edge policy details are supported.

claims.claim: The Purview path to sensitive service domain groups is Data loss prevention > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Endpoint DLP settings > Browser and domain restrictions to sensitive data > Sensitive service domain groups.
claims.quote: Data loss prevention > Settings (gear icon in the upper left hand corner) > Data Loss Prevention > Endpoint DLP settings > Browser and domain restrictions to sensitive data > Sensitive service domain groups.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <name> -EndpointDlpLocation <locations> is the automation counterpart for configuring the sensitive service domain groups and restrictions in this row.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. DLP policies contain DLP rules that identify, monitor, and protect sensitive information.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api to null: no equivalent automation for sensitive service domain groups was found in searches for 'sensitive service domain groups PowerShell' and 'sensitive service domain Set- DLP PowerShell'. Remove this call from the rendered row. If retained in prose, label it only as creating an Endpoint DLP policy container, not configuring domains or blocking rules; -EndpointDlpLocation selects user accounts and requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator membership. Retain the documented Purview UI procedure for domain-group configuration.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that the same enumerated sidepane DLP settings govern Writing Assistance.
claims.quote: Searched: "Writing Assistance" "DLP" policies Edge; "sensitive service domain groups" "PowerShell". Read MC1146821, ComposeInlineEnabled and Copilot Chat in Edge and Access to Page Content: the notice confirms DLP blocking generally, not a feature-specific mapping of these settings.

claims.claim: The Learn pages cited by this briefing do not describe the implementation of enterprise data protection specifically for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge Writing Assistance Rewrite Copilot ComposeInlineEnabled licensing price meter limits enterprise data protection. Read all five cited Learn pages and Manage Copilot Chat; general Copilot EDP descriptions were found, but no feature-specific implementation in the cited pages.

claims.claim: Any page not covered by a DLP rule or Edge policy is open to Writing Assistance.
claims.quote: Searched: "Writing Assistance" "Edge" supported text fields availability restrictions; "Writing Assistance" "DLP" policies Edge. Read ComposeInlineEnabled and MC1146821; neither guarantees every otherwise-unblocked page, and the policy reference qualifies use by feature availability.
claims.fix: Replace 'any page not covered by a DLP rule or Edge policy is open to it' with 'eligible users can use the writing features in supported web editing fields, subject to feature availability and other applicable policies'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/composeinlineenabled. Do not present DLP and Edge policy coverage as an exhaustive list of availability conditions.
